info.title: MemberSuite REST API
info.description:
The MemberSuite REST API exposes the association management system as one deployable web app per
feature module. Every module shares the conventions below.

### Authentication

All endpoints except `/about` require an `Authorization` header carrying an access token. Requests
without one are rejected with **401**, as are requests whose token lacks the security rights for the
record being touched — check both the token and the user's security settings when you see a 401.

### Tenants

Routes ending in `{tenantid}` are scoped to a single association. The tenant id is the numeric
association identifier, and it must match the partition the token was issued for. Routes that take an
`{id}` instead resolve the tenant from the record itself.

### Searching

Collection endpoints take an MSQL statement in `msql`, plus `page` (zero-based) and `pageSize`.
MSQL is MemberSuite's SQL-like query language, for example:

    SELECT ID, Name FROM Committee WHERE IsActive = true ORDER BY Name

A search returns only the fields the statement selects, not the full record. To discover the fields
and validation rules for a type, call its `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint.

### Creating and updating

* **POST** creates a record. Do **not** send `id` or `systemTimestamp` — either one makes the request
  fail with **409 Conflict**. Audit fields (`createdBy`, `createdDate`, `lastModifiedBy`,
  `lastModifiedDate`) are assigned by the server and ignored if supplied. A successful create returns
  **201** with the new `id` and a `Location` header.
* **PUT** replaces a record in full. Any field you omit is cleared, so read the record first and send
  it back with your changes applied. If you include `id` it must match the id in the URI.
* **DELETE** removes a record by id.

### Custom fields

Associations add their own fields to most objects, and those fields do **not** appear in the schemas
below - the schema shows the standard fields only. Send a custom field as a top-level property named
after the field itself, alongside the standard ones:

    { "name": "Finance Committee", "isActive": true, "MeetingRoom__c": "Boardroom" }

Call the object's `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint to discover which custom fields an association
has configured and what type each expects. A custom field of type Document or Image is sent under
`<FieldName>_Contents` instead, as an object carrying `filecontents` (base-64), `filename` and
`filetype`.

### Concurrency and caching

Endpoints that return a single record support conditional requests: send the `etag` from a previous
response back in `If-None-Match` and you will get **304** if nothing has changed. An update that
collides with someone else's change returns **409** — re-read the record and retry.

### Long-running requests

Send `Asynchronous: true` on a POST, PUT or DELETE to queue the work instead of waiting. The response
is **202 Accepted** with a `Location` header pointing at
`/{module}/v{version}/asyncstatus/{id}`, which you can poll for the outcome.

### Media types

Requests and responses are JSON with camel-cased property names. Ask for `application/hal+json` to
receive HATEOAS `_links` alongside each record.

get.summary: Reports the health and build of the Platform REST service.
get.description:
Requires no access token, so it is safe to use as a load balancer health check. The response carries the
            running assembly version and its build timestamp, and lists the XML documentation files Swagger loaded its
            descriptions from - an empty list there means this deployment is publishing an undocumented API.

get.summary: Returns the settings a client needs before anyone has signed in.
get.description:
Gives an application the association's identity and the details it must know to authenticate and
            display figures correctly: the user pool and client id to sign in against, the base currency, and
            the time zone. Read it at startup. It is not a search and it takes no MSQL - the association is
            found from the tenant id alone.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association whose settings are wanted.

404.description: No association exists with that tenant identifier.

get.summary: Searches AssociationConfigurationContainers with an MSQL query.
get.description:
Runs an MSQL statement against the AssociationConfigurationContainers belonging to one association and
            returns a single page of results. Only the fields your statement selects are returned, not the whole
            record, so fetch the full AssociationConfigurationContainer by id once you know which one you want. Call
            associationconfigurationcontainers/description/{tenantId} to see which fields are available to
            select and filter on.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association whose AssociationConfigurationContainers should be searched.

parameters.name: msql
parameters.description: The MSQL statement to run, for example SELECT ID, Name FROM AssociationConfigurationContainer.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the page to return.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of records to return per page.

200.description: A page of matching AssociationConfigurationContainer records.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

403.description: The token is valid, but this user is not permitted to read AssociationConfigurationContainers.

get.summary: Describes the fields and validation rules of the AssociationConfigurationContainer object.
get.description:
Returns the metadata for AssociationConfigurationContainer: each field, its data type, whether it is
            required, and the values any picklist accepts, including the custom fields this association has
            configured. Use it to work out what a create or update payload may contain, and which field names an MSQL
            statement can select.

parameters.name: tenantid
parameters.description: Identifier of the association whose configuration should be described.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

403.description: The token is valid, but this user is not permitted to read AssociationConfigurationContainers.

get.description:
Returns the complete AssociationConfigurationContainer record. The response carries an etag; send
            it back in an If-None-Match header on a later request to receive 304 Not Modified when the
            record has not changed since.

parameters.description: Identifier of the AssociationConfigurationContainer to retrieve.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

403.description: The token is valid, but this user is not permitted to read this AssociationConfigurationContainer.

Replaces the record in full, so send the complete AssociationConfigurationContainer: any field you leave
            out is cleared. Read the record first, apply your changes, and send the result back. If you include
            id it must match the id in the URL.

parameters.description: Identifier of the AssociationConfigurationContainer to replace.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

            attempt to modify an existing record and fails with 409 Conflict. The server assigns the audit
            fields. Call associationconfigurationcontainers/description/{tenantId} for the fields this object
            accepts and which of them are required. Send an Asynchronous: true header to queue the work
            instead of waiting for it.

post.summary: Reports whether a username already has a sign-in account with the identity provider.
post.description:
Lets a signup or sign-in screen branch before asking for a password: an existing account means offer
            sign-in, no account means offer registration. It answers only whether the account exists and reveals
            nothing else about it.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to check within.

400.description: No username was supplied.

get.summary: Returns an association's acronym.
get.description:
Needed by sign-in pages that must name or brand the association before anyone has authenticated, so
            it is answerable from the tenant id alone.

404.description: No association exists with that identifier.

post.summary: Signs a portal user in and returns their tokens.
post.description:
The main portal sign-in. Returns the id, access and refresh tokens for the user; put the id token in
            the Authorization header of subsequent calls, and exchange the refresh token at
            refreshtoken when it expires.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to sign in to.

400.description: The username or password was missing.

401.description: The credentials were not accepted.

post.summary: Completes a portal user's sign-in through the identity provider's hosted login.
post.description:
For a portal that signs its users in with the identity provider's hosted login and exchanges the code itself.
            Call this after the sign-in: it points the user's context parameters at this association. Then refresh the
            tokens; the new ones carry the association. The user must be an active portal user of the association.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the user signed in to.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description:
The identity provider's ID for the user who signed in - the "sub" of the token the hosted
            login issued, not the MemberSuite portal user ID (query string).

400.description: The partition key or the user ID was missing or not valid.

403.description: No active portal user of this association has that identity provider ID.

patch.summary: Sets a new password using the hash from a reset link.
patch.description:
Completes a forgotten-password flow: the hash comes from the link the user was emailed and stands in
            for their old password, which they no longer know. The hash is single-use and expires. To change a
            password the user does know, use changePassword.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the user belongs to.

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: The reset hash and the new password.

400.description: The hash was missing, already used, expired, or the new password was rejected.

post.summary: Checks a username and password without signing anyone in.
post.description:
Verifies credentials and issues no token, so use it to re-confirm a password before a sensitive change.
            To actually sign a user in, use loginUser/{tenantId}.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the user belongs to.

400.description: The username or password was missing.

401.description: The credentials were not accepted.

post.summary: Signs a user in and returns a ready-made Authorization header value.
post.description:
One of three sign-in endpoints that differ only in what they return. This one returns the string
            Bearer <token> as plain text, ready to copy straight into an Authorization
            header - convenient from a shell or a test client. msc_authdata/{tenantId} and
            authdata/{tenantId} return the token data instead. Prefer loginUser/{tenantId} for new
            work, since it also returns the refresh token.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to sign in to.

400.description: The credentials were missing or not accepted.

get.summary: Issues a token for an association's anonymous portal user.
get.description:
Public portal pages act as a designated anonymous user rather than as nobody, and this issues that
            user's token so such a page can call the API before anyone signs in. Returns the string
            Bearer <token> as plain text. Associations that have not enabled anonymous access answer
            403.

403.description: This association does not permit anonymous access.

post.summary: Retired. It reset a user's password on an administrator's behalf.
post.description:
This endpoint is no longer supported and always answers 410 Gone without doing anything. It
            remains routed so that existing callers get a clear answer rather than a 404. Remove your calls to it.

410.description: The endpoint is retired and performs no work.

post.summary: Changes a user's password, given their current one.
post.description:
For a user who knows their existing password. Someone who has forgotten it goes through
            resetPasswordWithHash/{tenantId} instead. tenantId is optional here: omit it and the
            association is taken from the access token.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association. Optional; taken from the token when omitted.

400.description: The current password was wrong, or the new one was rejected by the password policy.

post.summary: Changes a user's password, taking the association from the access token.
post.description:
The original form of changePassword, kept for existing callers. It behaves the same but cannot
            be told which association to act on, so it always uses the one on the token. Prefer
            changePassword for new work.

400.description: The current password was wrong, or the new one was rejected by the password policy.

post.summary: Retired. It completed a forgotten-password flow with a confirmation code.
post.description:
This endpoint is no longer supported and always answers 410 Gone without doing anything. It
            remains routed so that existing callers get a clear answer rather than a 404. Use
            resetPasswordWithHash/{tenantId} instead.

410.description: The endpoint is retired and performs no work.

post.summary: Verifies a JWT and reports what it contains.
post.description:
Checks the token's signature and expiry and returns its claims, so a downstream service can trust a
            token it was handed without holding the signing keys itself. Verification only - nothing is issued and
            no session is created.

400.description: No token was supplied.

401.description: The token's signature was invalid, or it has expired.

get.summary: Exchanges a one-time GUID for the legacy token cached against it.
get.description:
The far end of the legacy single sign-on handshake: the browser is redirected to the portal carrying a
            GUID, and the portal calls this to collect the token. Treat the GUID as a credential - anyone holding
            it can collect the token. Use bearerTokenSSO for the JWT-based flow.

parameters.name: tokenGUID
parameters.description: The one-time GUID from the sign-on redirect.

parameters.name: partitionKey
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the token belongs to.

400.description: The GUID was missing or not a valid GUID.

401.description: The GUID does not correspond to a cached token.

post.summary: Bridges a legacy sign-in into Portal 5.
post.description:
Part of the legacy single sign-on bridge. It accepts a form post rather than JSON, exchanges the
            legacy token in it for a session, stores that session against a one-time GUID, and redirects the
            browser to the portal carrying the GUID rather than the token itself. Because it ends in a
            redirect it is meant to be posted to by a browser, not called from code; the portal then
            collects the token with GET /regularSSO.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The form post carrying the legacy token.

403.description: The legacy token was missing, expired or not accepted.

post.summary: Signs a user in and returns the raw token data rather than a header string.
post.description:
One of three sign-in endpoints that differ only in the shape of what they return.
            authtoken/{tenantId} returns a ready-made Bearer … string, this one returns the token
            data as an object, and authdata/{tenantId} returns the same data typed. Prefer
            loginUser/{tenantId} for new work.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to sign in to.

400.description: The credentials were missing or not accepted.

post.summary: Signs a user in and returns their token data.
post.description:
One of three sign-in endpoints that differ only in the shape of what they return.
            authtoken/{tenantId} returns a ready-made Bearer … string and
            msc_authdata/{tenantId} returns an untyped object. Prefer loginUser/{tenantId} for new
            work.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to sign in to.

400.description: The credentials were missing or not accepted.

get.summary: Returns the anonymous portal user an association uses for unauthenticated visitors.
get.description:
Public portal pages act as a designated anonymous user rather than as nobody. This returns that user,
            so a page can tell what it is permitted to see. Associations that have not enabled anonymous access
            have none.

403.description: This association does not permit anonymous access.

get.summary: Clears one user's cached authentication token.
get.description:
Tokens are cached to avoid re-authenticating on every call, so a change to a user's credentials or
            permissions is not seen until the cache entry expires. Flushing it forces the next call to
            re-authenticate. An operational tool, not part of any normal flow.

parameters.name: userType
parameters.description: Which user pool the account belongs to.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address of the account whose token should be dropped.

400.description: No email address was supplied.

get.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh set of tokens, taking it from the query string.
get.description:
Identical in effect to the POST form of refreshtoken, but the token travels in the URL, where
            it is liable to end up in browser history, proxy logs and referrer headers. Prefer the POST form; this
            exists for callers that cannot send a body.

400.description: The refresh token was missing.

401.description: The refresh token was rejected or has expired.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh set of tokens.
post.description:
Access tokens are short-lived; call this with the refresh token from sign-in to get a new set without
            asking the user for their password again. A refresh token that has itself expired cannot be renewed -
            sign the user in again. The GET form of this route takes the token in the query string instead, which
            puts a credential in the URL; prefer this POST.

400.description: The refresh token was missing.

401.description: The refresh token was rejected or has expired.

post.summary: Retired. It started a forgotten-password flow.
post.description:
This endpoint is no longer supported and always answers 410 Gone without doing anything. It
            remains routed so that existing callers get a clear answer rather than a 404. Remove your calls to it.

410.description: The endpoint is retired and performs no work.

get.summary: Reminds a caller that usernames are email addresses.
get.description:
Kept so that a "forgot my username" link has somewhere to go. It performs no lookup and sends no
            email: usernames are email addresses, so it returns that sentence for any input, including an address
            that belongs to nobody.

post.summary: Bridges a legacy password reset into Portal 5.
post.description:
Part of the legacy single sign-on bridge into Portal 5. It accepts a form post rather than JSON,
            exchanges the legacy token in it for a session, stores that session against a one-time GUID, and
            redirects the browser to the portal's reset page carrying the GUID. Because it ends in a redirect it is meant to
            be posted to by a browser, not called from code; retrieve the stored token with
            bearerTokenSSO.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The form post carrying the legacy token.

403.description: The legacy token was missing, expired or not accepted.

            exchanges the legacy token in it for a session, stores that session against a one-time GUID, and
            redirects the browser to the portal's change-password page carrying the GUID. Because it ends in a redirect it is meant to
            be posted to by a browser, not called from code; retrieve the stored token with
            bearerTokenSSO.

parameters.name: value

403.description: The legacy token was missing, expired or not accepted.

            exchanges the legacy token in it for a session, stores that session against a one-time GUID, and

parameters.description: The form post carrying the legacy token.

403.description: The legacy token was missing, expired or not accepted.

post.summary: Signs a user in, caches their JWT, and redirects the browser to the portal.
post.description:
A single sign-on entry point: it authenticates the credentials, stores the resulting JWT against a
            one-time GUID, and redirects to the portal carrying that GUID rather than the token itself, so the
            token never appears in a URL or a browser history. The portal then exchanges the GUID at
            bearerTokenSSO. Because it ends in a redirect it is meant to be posted to by a browser.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association to sign in to.

400.description: The credentials were missing or not accepted.

post.summary: Stores an already-issued JWT against a one-time GUID for single sign-on.
post.description:
For callers that have already authenticated the user themselves and hold a JWT: this caches it and
            returns the GUID to put in a sign-on link, which the portal exchanges at bearerTokenSSO. Unlike
            storeJWTTokenForUser/{tenantId} it verifies no credentials and issues no redirect.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the token belongs to.

400.description: The payload was missing, or the partition key was not valid.

get.summary: Exchanges a one-time GUID for the JWT cached against it.
get.description:
The far end of the single sign-on handshake: the portal receives a GUID in its URL and calls this to
            collect the token. Treat the GUID as a credential - anyone holding it can collect the token.

parameters.name: tokenGUID
parameters.description: The one-time GUID from the sign-on link.

parameters.name: partitionKey
parameters.description: Identifier of the association the token belongs to.

400.description: The GUID was missing or not a valid GUID.

401.description: The GUID does not correspond to a cached token.

post.summary: Signs a user in without naming an association, and returns an Authorization header value.
post.description:
The tenant-less sign-in: it works out which association the username belongs to before
            authenticating, so a caller that does not know the tenant id can still sign in. A username that
            exists in more than one association cannot be disambiguated here - use the tenant-scoped
            authtoken/{tenantId} for that. Returns the string Bearer <token> as plain
            text, with no refresh token; use authtoken_alt when you need one.

400.description: The credentials were missing, not accepted, or the association could not be determined.

post.summary: Signs a console user in without naming an association, and returns the raw token.
post.description:
Behaves like authtoken - it determines the association from the username first - but returns the
            bare token rather than a Bearer … header string. Added for the EventFarm integration, which
            needs the token itself.

400.description: The credentials were missing, not accepted, or the association could not be determined.

post.summary: Signs a user in without naming an association, returning the full token set.
post.description:
The same tenant-less sign-in as authtoken, but it returns the whole token response -
            including the refresh token - rather than a single header string. Prefer it when the caller needs
            to refresh the session later rather than signing in again.

400.description: The credentials were missing, not accepted, or the association could not be determined.

post.description:
Called by Stripe, not by your own code. It verifies the signature on the incoming event against
            the payout webhook secret and records the payout against the association, so settlement can be
            reconciled. An event whose signature does not verify is rejected. Stripe retries on any non-2xx
            response, so the same event can arrive more than once.

post.summary: Receives Stripe charge notifications.
post.description:
Called by Stripe, not by your own code. It verifies the signature on the incoming event and
            applies the charge outcome - succeeded, failed, refunded, disputed - to the matching MemberSuite
            payment. This is how a payment taken asynchronously reaches the ledger. Stripe retries on any
            non-2xx response, so the same event can arrive more than once.

400.description: The payload was unreadable, or its signature did not verify.

post.summary: Receives Stripe payment method notifications.
post.description:
Called by Stripe, not by your own code. It handles automatic card updates: when an issuer
            reissues a card, Stripe supplies the new details and this keeps the stored payment method in step,
            so recurring billing does not start failing on a card that expired. It also handles payment
            methods being attached to or detached from a customer. Stripe retries on any non-2xx response.

400.description: The payload was unreadable, or its signature did not verify.
